metadata.contentSnippet: The first wave of artists has been announced for the 2027 Cambridge Folk Festival.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Father John Misty, Billy Bragg and The Waterboys to headline Cambridge Folk Festival
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The first wave of artists has been announced for the 2027 Cambridge Folk Festival. Father John Misty, Billy Bragg and The Waterboys will headline the long-running event, set to return to Cherry Hinton Hall from July 30 to August 1. Organisers have promised another "unforgettable" weekend of music and community, blending world-class headliners with emerging talent. A spokesperson for the Cambridge Folk Festival team said: "We can't wait to share three unforgettable days of music with you. "Whether you're a long-time festival regular or joining us for the first time, there's something very special about being part of Cambridge Folk Festival." Billy Bragg (Image: Cambridge Folk Festival) The full line-up already includes a mix of established and rising artists, with Karine Polwart, Eliza Carthy & The Restitution, Fanny Lumsden, Tamikrest, Dug, D.K. Harrell, Seamus Fogarty, Madalitso Band and Charm of Finches set to perform. Organisers said more names will be revealed in the coming months. The 2027 edition will feature two main stages, Club Corner, street performances and plenty of opportunities to discover new talent. Fans are encouraged to secure their tickets early, with tier one tickets already on sale. Day tickets will be available from November 27. A spokesperson for the festival team said: "Join us from Friday 30 July to Sunday 1 August 2027 at our much-loved home of Cherry Hinton Hall." "Tickets are on sale now, so secure your place and start planning your summer with us."

metadata.title: Judge tells jurors psychotic intent to kill is still intent to kill in train trial
metadata.contentSnippet: The judge in the trial of a knifeman accused of the attempted murder of 10 people on a London-bound train has told jurors that a psychotic intent to kill is still an intent to kill.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Judge tells jurors psychotic intent to kill is still intent to kill in train trial
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The judge in the trial of a knifeman accused of the attempted murder of 10 people on a London-bound train has told jurors that a psychotic intent to kill is still an intent to kill. Anthony Williams, 33, denies attempting to murder 10 people on the train between Peterborough and Huntingdon, where it made an unscheduled stop on November 1 last year. He also denies the attempted murders of three people in Peterborough on October 31 and of a 17-year-old boy at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London in the early hours of November 1. The judge, Mr Justice Calver KC, said Williams accepted carrying out the attacks but jurors must consider whether he intended to kill. He said psychiatrists instructed by the prosecution and defence agree that the defendant “at the relevant time was suffering from an acute psychosis as a result of his schizophrenia”. Giving his legal directions at Cambridge Crown Court on Thursday, he told jurors to consider all of the evidence in the case and “it is for you, not the psychiatrists, to decide whether the defendant, in fact, intended to kill a particular victim”. The judge said that, in his evidence, psychiatrist Dr Bernard Chin, who was instructed by the defence, referred to things Williams told him during clinical interviews and that he learned from an assessment carried out the day after the attacks on the LNER train. These included things such as “people sent by the devil wanted to attack the defendant and cars were going to run him over” and “there was a conspiracy these people were accusing him of being a nonce – that being a paedophile”, the judge said. The judge said Dr Chin also recounted the defendant relaying that “during the events it was all real, he was attacking real people with real knives” and “I just needed to protect myself, it was me or them”. The judge said that what Williams said to Dr Chin, and to the psychiatrist who assessed Williams on November 2 2025, is “not in itself evidence” but Dr Chin was permitted to repeat it in court so jurors could understand the factual basis on which he reached his clinical opinion. “Attempted murder requires a specific intent to kill,” the judge said. “While the defendant’s mental illness is one factor which you may take into account… a psychotic intent to kill or a drunken intent to kill is still an intent to kill.” He said that a “person who is mentally ill, acting psychotically under a delusion, can still form an intent to kill”. “If someone suffers a delusion that a person is the devil and stabs them in a particular case with the purpose of killing them, they will still possess the intention to kill despite their motive being entirely driven by their irrational illness,” the judge said. He said it is “agreed that lawful self-defence does not arise in this case”. He said Williams has pleaded guilty to wounding with intent to cause really serious bodily harm in respect of 12 victims and attempting to do so to two of those in Peterborough on October 31. The judge said jurors need to ask themselves if they were “sure that at the time of the attack on the relevant victim the defendant intended to kill that victim”. Christopher Paxton KC began his prosecution closing speech by repeating some of the defendant’s words. The barrister began his speech: “I’ve got a knife and I’m not afraid to use it. “You’re all going to die today. “Do you want to die? “I’m going to kill you. “I will stab you if you don’t move. “You need to let me through. “I’m not going to leave anyone. “Members of the jury, all those words from one man, the defendant, with one intention – to kill.” Mr Paxton said the defendant’s intention to kill “lay bare not just in his words, some of which I’ve reminded you of, but in the slashes and stabs he inflicted not on the devil but on real people”. “People going about their lawful business as you might,” he said. “Walking with a friend, going to a cashpoint and travelling on a train. “People as young as 14 and as old as 73. “Striking at them, not with his fists with punches or feet with kicks and stamps, but with a knife, a large knife that the defendant Mr Williams took, that defendant Mr Williams selected, that defendant Mr Williams chose.” He continued: “You may think it’s a miracle that no-one died at the hands of the defendant that Halloween weekend but it’s not for the want of the defendant trying, that’s for sure.” The trial continues.

metadata.title: Paedophile who asked 'girl' for school uniform photos pictured for first time
metadata.contentSnippet: A paedophile posed as a woman in an attempt to get sexualised images from what he thought was a 12-year-old girl.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Paedophile who asked 'girl' for school uniform photos pictured for first time
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A paedophile from Cambridgeshire posed as a woman in an attempt to get sexualised images from what he thought was a 12-year-old girl. Callum Walker began speaking to the girl, who was actually an undercover police officer, through the online chat platform Kik on 25 November 2024. Walker, who was posing as a 30-year-old woman, turned the conversation sexual and asked for “cheeky” photos in her school uniform. He also asked to make sure they were “a tad nude, like bra and underwear.” The 32-year-old also suggested she touch herself inappropriately and they continued speaking until 19 December of that year. Walker was arrested at his home on January 8, 2025. On Tuesday (November 17), at Cambridge Crown Court, Walker, of Guernsey Way, Littleport, was jailed for two years and six months. He pleaded guilty at an earlier hearing to attempt to cause/incite a girl under 13 to engage in sexual activity – penetration, and attempted sexual communications with a child. He was also placed on the Sex Offenders Register indefinitely and handed a ten-year sexual harm prevention order. DC Kev Foxcroft, who investigated, said: "The fact Walker was willing to pose as a woman to gain the trust of what he thought was a 12-year-old girl was seen as an aggravating by the court. “We will do all we can to bring those who look to abuse children to justice." metadata.title: Knifeman attacked only men during Hunts to Peterborough train stabbing, court told
metadata.contentSnippet: A knifeman who stabbed 10 people on a London-bound train attacked only men on the service, a court heard.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Knifeman attacked only men during Hunts to Peterborough train stabbing, court told
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A knifeman who stabbed 10 people on a London-bound train attacked only men on the service, a court heard. Anthony Williams, 33, denies attempting to murder 10 people on the train between Peterborough and Huntingdon, where it made an unscheduled stop on November 1 last year. The defendant was suffering psychosis as a result of his schizophrenia at the time, jurors at Cambridge Crown Court have been told. Psychiatrist Dr Bernard Chin said in evidence that the defendant had said he feared “people sent by the devil wanted to attack” him. In his closing speech to jurors, prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said that after boarding the LNER train at Peterborough and drinking alcohol “Mr Williams launches his attack, attacking 10 men, only men, in minutes”. “Did Mr Williams see the devil only as a man?” the prosecutor said. He said that “if the defendant thought the men he attacked were the devil… he would want them dead, wouldn’t he”. He noted that Williams did not attack people on the platform but did so on board the train. “If there’s a conspiracy by the devil, if it was Mr Williams saying ‘it’s me or them’, it’s easier to kill people if they are trapped,” said Mr Paxton. “It’s easier to try and kill people if they have nowhere to go.” Williams also denies the attempted murders of three people in Peterborough on October 31 and of a boy on a DLR train approaching Pontoon Dock station in London in the early hours of November 1. CCTV footage issued by British Transport Police showing Anthony Williams boarding a Thameslink train at Stevenage station (Image: BTP/Press Association) Mr Paxton said the “deadly attack” on the boy on the DLR train, Isaiah Idris who was then aged 17 and is now 18, “only failed it seems because of the intervention” of another passenger and because Mr Idris moved along the carriage. “If Mr Williams thought he was fighting the devil his intention would surely be to kill and slay the devil, to use the expression ‘it was me or them’,” said Mr Paxton. The judge, Mr Justice Calver KC, said Williams accepted carrying out the attacks but jurors must consider whether he intended to kill. The judge, giving his legal directions on Thursday, told jurors that a “psychotic intent to kill or a drunken intent to kill is still an intent to kill”. He said that a “person who is mentally ill, acting psychotically under a delusion, can still form an intent to kill”. “If someone suffers a delusion that a person is the devil and stabs them in a particular case with the purpose of killing them, they will still possess the intention to kill despite their motive being entirely driven by their irrational illness,” the judge said. He said it is “agreed that lawful self-defence does not arise in this case”. The trial continues.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A shoplifter has been jailed after breaching a court order and going on a three-day stealing spree. Joshua Preece, 21, was sentenced to eight months at Huntingdon Magistrates’ Court on November 12 after admitting four counts of theft from a shop and two breaches of a criminal behaviour order (CBO). The thefts took place in Peterborough between October 30 and November 1, targeting M&S and Next at Brotherhood Retail Park and a BP filling station in Bretton. He also breached his two-year CBO by entering the Bretton Centre on October 26 and 31. PC Sam Malton said: "These court orders give us greater powers to tackle prolific offenders such as Preece, as we are able to arrest for every breach and put them before the courts." Preece, of no fixed address, was arrested in Millfield.

metadata.title: REVEALED: Full list of Cambs flats with ‘potentially unsafe cladding’
metadata.contentSnippet: All of the Cambridgeshire buildings still waiting for “potentially unsafe cladding” to be replaced have been revealed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: REVEALED: Full list of Cambs flats with ‘potentially unsafe cladding’
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: All of the Cambridgeshire buildings still waiting for “potentially unsafe cladding” to be replaced have been revealed. The Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority’s board is recommended to approve a new plan to replace cladding on residential buildings at next week’s meeting. Earlier this month, the CPCA’s growth committee heard the updated plan will address key risks, including landlord reluctance, contractor capacity and developer disputes. In 2025, following the second phase of the inquiry into the Grenfell Tower fire, which killed 72 people, the government introduced targets for cladding to be replaced on residential flat buildings. For medium-rise buildings – those between 11 and 18 metres – this is the end of 2031, but for high-rises over 18m it is the end of 2029. The Local Democracy Reporting Service revealed the names of the ten high-rise buildings waiting for cladding to be replaced last month, which include the flats attached to Cambridge Fire Station. A request under the Freedom of Information Act has now revealed the names of all of the buildings in Cambridgeshire, including the 64 medium-rise buildings which need cladding replaced. A report to the CPCA has noted that a few buildings have come in and out of scope after being assessed in detail. It said a total of 150 medium-rise buildings were assessed – with 62 needing remediation and two currently undergoing remediation and a further 39 buildings yet to be assessed. The report specified that “potentially unsafe cladding” covers external wall systems which could involve cladding types, insulation and cavity barriers. All ten high-rises are in Cambridge, as previously reported, as are the majority of the medium-rise buildings with 45 in the city council’s boundaries. Three are in Huntingdonshire – all on Princes Street in Huntingdon – 13 are in Peterborough and three are in South Cambs in the Orchard Park development in Cambridge. The CPCA has emphasised that just because a building needs cladding replaced, this does not mean it is unsafe to live in. Mitigations may be put in place such as an upgraded fire alarm system to allow residents to evacuate simultaneously instead of staying put. A CPCA spokesperson said that the Local Remediation Acceleration Plan is reviewed every year after being first published in July 2025, in line with the government’s national remediation plan. They said: “Figures for remediation are compiled at intervals and reported to our Growth Committee and Board. “The latest for medium rise buildings show that five buildings have had remediation completed, two are undergoing remediation, and 14 have started or are due to start shortly. Regulators are working with those responsible for each building to move them forward. “The Combined Authority funds the Remediation Manager and Inspector posts at Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service. They assess buildings and work with those responsible to get works done, and where they are not meeting their obligations, regulators will take appropriate action. “Requiring remediation does not mean a building is unsafe to live in. Each building is assessed by a qualified fire engineer through an external wall report, and mitigating measures, such as changes to the fire alarm system, may be in place while works are planned and carried out. That process, from first reports to completed works, can take 18 months to two years. “Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service has fire safety advice for residents of buildings undergoing remediation: metadata.title: Cambridgeshire fire service warns of rising battery fires ahead of Christmas
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service warns of lithium-ion battery fire risks during Black Friday and Christmas sales, urging safe charging and recycling.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire fire service warns of rising battery fires ahead of Christmas
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service has warned of the fire risks posed by rechargeable batteries ahead of the Christmas shopping season. It is urging shoppers to take care when buying and using electrical items during Black Friday, Christmas and the January sales, especially lithium-ion devices such as phones, tablets, laptops and e-scooters. An electric scooter that has been involved in a fire caused by its battery. (Image: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service) The warning comes as battery-related fires rise, with more incidents recorded this year than in previous years. James Ball, group commander and head of community fire safety at Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service, said: "We have seen a consistent increase in fires involving batteries every year since 2019. "In the last month alone, our crews in Cambridge have responded to three fires involving batteries, one of which involved significant damage to a home. A housefire that was caused by a battery fire. (Image: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service) "Fortunately, no one was injured in any of the incidents." He said electrical devices are part of daily life and popular gifts during seasonal sales. Group Commander Ball said: "When buying electrical items, particularly batteries and chargers, always use a reputable retailer and follow the manufacturer’s instructions. "Only use chargers and batteries recommended for your device, avoid charging them overnight or when you’re out of the house." The fire service is also reminding residents to dispose of batteries properly because batteries thrown in household bins can start fires in refuse lorries and waste facilities. Group Commander Ball said: "It is also really important to dispose of batteries safely. "Never put them in household bins. "Although it is an additional thing to remember, it is vitally important to take any kind of battery to a local recycling centre. "Many local shops and supermarkets also have recycling bins for batteries, so please consider taking any used batteries with you when you go shopping." He also urged people to make electrical safety part of their nightly routine to reduce the risk of fire. Group Commander Ball said: "Planning a good bedtime routine can also help prevent a fire. "Make sure plugs are switched off and items are not left charging overnight. "A few small steps can make a big difference in keeping your family safe during this festive season. "So, as you shop, remember to Take Charge and Be Safe."

metadata.title: Refreshed strategy to support Cambridgeshire's unpaid carers
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire County Council launches an All-Age Carers Strategy on November 19, strengthening support for unpaid, young, young adult and parent carers.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Refreshed strategy to support Cambridgeshire's unpaid carers
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A refreshed strategy from Cambridgeshire County Council aims to better support unpaid carers of all ages. They launched the updated All-Age Carers Strategy on November 19 to mark Carers Rights Day and renew its support for unpaid carers across the county. The strategy recognises people who care for ill, disabled or otherwise vulnerable family members, friends and neighbours. Councillor Graham Wilson, chair of the adults and health committee, said: "Unpaid carers make an enormous contribution to communities across Cambridgeshire, providing vital support to family members, friends and neighbours, often alongside work, education and other responsibilities. "We know that caring can be incredibly rewarding, but it can also have a significant impact on a person's health, wellbeing and finances. "Through this refreshed strategy, we want carers of all ages to feel recognised, valued and supported. "That includes young carers, young adult carers, parent carers and adult carers, each of whom may need different types of support at different stages of their lives." The strategy aims to improve wellbeing, strengthen families and help people live independently for longer. The 2021 Census recorded five million unpaid carers across England and Wales, while evidence suggests caring is becoming more intensive for people juggling work, education and family life. The updated strategy was developed in collaboration with unpaid carers, families, health partners, carer support organisations, and voluntary and community groups. Its seven priorities include better access to advice and support, improved emotional wellbeing, stronger health and social care links, and help for young, parent and vulnerable carers. It also makes specific commitments to young carers, young adult carers, parent carers and adult carers. The strategy will focus on identifying and supporting young, young adult and parent carers so they can thrive while balancing their responsibilities. The launch comes as the council continues to invest in support for unpaid carers through partnerships with local organisations and services. The council’s Bridgit platform has reached more than 11,000 unpaid carers across Cambridgeshire, including people who did not previously see themselves as carers. Cllr Wilson said: "This includes ensuring young carers and young adult carers have the support they need to achieve their potential and get the best start in life, while making sure all carers can access the information, advice and practical help they need. "Carers Rights Day is an opportunity to recognise and thank unpaid carers for everything they do, while reminding them that they are not alone and that support is available whenever they need it." The council works with Caring Together, Centre 33, Pinpoint and Making Space to provide advice, emotional support, training, peer networks and practical help. The strategy will shape future carers’ services in Cambridgeshire and guide the recommissioning of the county’s All-Age Carers Service. It also supports the council’s goal of building a healthy, fair and sustainable Cambridgeshire. Anyone regularly caring for a family member, friend or neighbour can find support and read the refreshed strategy on the council’s website.

metadata.title: Christmas lights hung upside down in Cambridgeshire town
metadata.contentSnippet: A council has responded after Christmas lights featuring baubles were hung upside down on lampposts in Huntingdon.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Christmas lights hung upside down in Cambridgeshire town
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A council has responded after Christmas lights featuring baubles were hung upside down on lampposts in a Cambridgeshire town. Eagle-eyed locals in Huntingdon were quick to spot that the festive lights had been installed incorrectly by staff. The illuminations, near the Market Square, are among the displays that will be switched on during an annual community event on November 28. Huntingdon Town Council confirmed it had been made aware some of the decorations were "currently experiencing a festive identity crisis". They were repaired on Wednesday (November 19), a spokesperson for the local authority said. In a statement, they added: "We're delighted that people are already paying such close attention to this year's new Christmas lights. "Unfortunately, three of our baubles were feeling a little topsy-turvy when they were installed, but the issue was identified and corrected. "We're pleased to report that all decorations are now the right way up and ready for the festive season ahead. "We're grateful to those who highlighted the issue and look forward to welcoming everyone to our Christmas Lights Switch On event on 28 November." Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: 'Would-be' robber who tried to steal mobility scooter from man in 70s pictured
metadata.contentSnippet: A would-be robber who attempted to steal a watch and a mobility scooter from an elderly man in Peterborough has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Would-be' robber who tried to steal mobility scooter from man in 70s pictured
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A "would-be" robber who tried to steal a watch and a mobility scooter from a man in Cambridgeshire has been jailed. Daadir Faragab, 39, was seen behaving erratically in the Peterborough city centre, making his way to Long Causeway. He spotted the victim on a mobility scooter and made a comment about the man’s watch before unsuccessfully trying to remove it from his wrist. He then grabbed the handlebars of the scooter and made remarks suggesting he would try to steal that instead. The victim, a man in his 70s, managed to get away and Faragab was arrested by nearby police officers. On Monday (November 16) at Cambridge Crown Court, Faragab, of Thorpe Meadows, Peterborough, admitted attempted robbery. He was sentenced to 13 months in prison. DC Lisa Flatters said: "To target an elderly man on a mobility scooter like this really is shocking, and his reported behaviour towards other members of the public that day was also very concerning. "I’m pleased there were police officers nearby and Faragab was quickly apprehended so he could face justice for his actions. "The victim was understandably shaken by the experience but thankfully escaped unharmed." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Historic church wall to be replaced after ‘extensive degradation’ beyond repair
metadata.contentSnippet: The wall around St Mary’s Church in St Neots is set to be replaced after it was found to have deteriorated to the point that “repair is not possible”.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Historic church wall to be replaced after ‘extensive degradation’ beyond repair
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. The wall around a listed church is set to be replaced after it was found to have deteriorated to the point that “repair is not possible”. Permission was granted to demolish the wall surrounding St Mary’s Church in St Neots by hand, keeping as much good brick as possible. A structural survey of the wall found it to be “generally in poor condition throughout, with extensive degradation of brickwork and mortar”. Vegetation was also seen to be growing on the wall which showed signs of “movement” and “evidence of previous inappropriate repairs”. A Section Of The Boundary Wall Around St Mary'S Church, St Neots. Credit: Google Maps A planning document from Huntingdonshire District Council said: “The structural engineer concluded that the walls are heavily degraded to an extent that repair is not possible and recommended the demolition and reconstruction of the affected sections.” An objection was raised by the council’s conservation officer who was concerned the wall’s replacement would “result in the loss of historic fabric” and “evidence of traditional construction methods and materials”. The officer said “insufficient information” was given to “justify this harm” and said the proposed use of modern materials and construction techniques “could adversely affect the character and appearance of the wall”. But after the plans were amended with a detailed method statement, the officer removed their objection and “accepted that the existing walls had reached the end of their lifespan”. A neighbour did not object but raised a number of concerns and said much of the wall’s deterioration was due to “previous repairs undertaken using cement-based mortar”. They said that “unless appropriate materials are utilised, a rebuilt wall could experience similar problems in the future”. They advocated for the use of traditional materials and construction techniques, including lime mortar, in line with “recognised conservation best practice”.

metadata.title: Glastonbury 2027 headliners and legends slot confirmed as line-up takes shape
metadata.contentSnippet: Glastonbury 2027 headliners Sam Fender, Harry Styles and Billie Eilish will play Worthy Farm from June 23-27, with Cher confirmed for the legends slot

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Glastonbury 2027 headliners and legends slot confirmed as line-up takes shape
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Glastonbury Festival has announced its three headliners for the 2027 event. Sam Fender, Harry Styles and Billie Eilish will all take to the famous Pyramid Stage during the weekend in June. It comes as Cher was confirmed to be taking the coveted legends slot that Shania Twain and the late Dolly Parton have previously graced. After a break in 2026, the event will return next year, June 23-27, at Worthy Farm in Pilton, Somerset. Styles, Fender and Eilish will be joined by acts Sombr, Sienna Spiro, Lily Allen, The Streets, Chase & Status, Kacey Musgraves, Primal Scream and Adéla. Fender will headline the first night, marking his second time at Glastonbury after last playing in 2022. 'As It Was' singer Styles will perform on Saturday before Eilish closes Glastonbury on the Sunday night. Discussing the 2027 festival, organiser Emily Eavis said: "We are so happy to be coming back after our fallow year and, as we head into winter after that peaceful period, we wanted to give you an early musical taster of what's to come at Glastonbury 2027 with this spread of incredible artists. "We can't wait to see you down here on Worthy Farm in June for some much-needed good times!" Glastonbury will kick off on Wednesday 23 June, with music starting on Friday 25 June. RECOMMENDED READING: Tickets for the 2027 festival sold out in just 42 minutes last month, with more demand than ever following a year off in 2026. The cost of tickets was at an all-time high at £408, including an additional £5 booking fee per ticket. Did you manage to get tickets to Glastonbury? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Martin Lewis warns shoppers why gift cards are the worst Christmas gifts of all
metadata.contentSnippet: Martin Lewis has highlighted the risks of Christmas gift cards, warning they can become worthless if a retailer goes bust or the voucher expires.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Martin Lewis warns shoppers why gift cards are the worst Christmas gifts of all
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Martin Lewis has issued a Christmas warning to shoppers thinking of buying gift cards, saying vouchers often become worthless if a retailer goes bust or the recipient fails to spend them before they expire. The Money Saving Expert said people should think carefully - gift cards are often seen as an easy option for Christmas because they allow friends and family to choose something from a shop they like. But Mr Lewis said shoppers should not assume vouchers are as safe as giving cash. He acknowledged that some people feel more comfortable giving a gift card than handing over money, saying: “Many find giving a gift card more socially acceptable than cash. “I get it. Cash gifts just are not very British. “Yes unfortunately, vouchers have risks.” One of the biggest dangers is that a retailer could go bust. If that happens, gift cards may no longer be accepted, meaning the recipient could lose the value of the present. Mr Lewis said: “If the store goes bust, gift vouchers usually become worthless.” He also warned that shoppers should check the expiry date before buying a voucher, as some have deadlines that may not be made clear enough. “Many have expiry dates, which often are not made clear enough,” he said. His advice was to consider how financially secure the retailer is and whether the recipient is likely to spend the voucher quickly. “So, think carefully about the likely financial strength of the retailer, and how quickly they'll be used,” he said. Mr Lewis suggested that shoppers who are unsure should choose cash instead. “If in doubt, cash, or money in the bank, is the ultimate gift voucher. It is totally flexible and usable anywhere.” This follows advice on his website Money Saving Expert, which says: "It's always better to give cash rather than a gift card – it's less risky and ensures the recipient will be able to buy some sort of present even if their favourite store goes under." The post continues: "Always remember gift cards and vouchers are likely to have expiry dates - check yours and make a note so you don't forget to use them in time." A review of 18 major retailers found that nine will restart the expiry countdown if customers make a balance enquiry, meaning shoppers could get more time without having to spend anything. Confused.com personal finance expert Tara Evans said: "Before you start your Christmas shopping, check whether you already have gift-card money you could put towards it. It is easy for a present to end up in a drawer or an old email and be forgotten about." The rules vary between shops, with some offering a fresh expiry period after a balance check, while others extend cards following a purchase. Boots and H&M, for example, restart the expiry period following a transaction or purchase. Other retailers offer longer-lasting vouchers. Apple and TK Maxx/Homesense gift cards have no expiry date, while Amazon cards are valid for 10 years from issue. Morrisons and ASOS give customers 24 months from purchase to use their gift cards, with no extension available.

metadata.title: Lidl confirms date they will cut vegetable prices to 9p ahead of Christmas
metadata.contentSnippet: Lidl has confirmed the exact date they will be slashing the price of some vegetables to just 9p ahead of Christmas.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Lidl confirms date they will cut vegetable prices to 9p ahead of Christmas
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Lidl has confirmed the exact date they will be slashing the price of some vegetables to just 9p ahead of Christmas. Supermarkets across the nation reduced vegetable prices last December and Lidl have pledged to do the same this year. The chain say that from Saturday December 19 bags of Christmas dinner trimmings like sprouts (500g) , potatoes (2kg), carrots (1kg) and parsnips (550g) will cost just 9p. The news comes after Aldi revealed their veg will be priced at just 8p, which is 1p cheaper than Lidl's offer. However Lidl claim to sell the cheapest Christmas dinner on the market, with a cost of £11.11 to feed a family of eight at £1.39 per person. This is led by their offer on a Birchwood British Small Turkey (3kg) which is priced at £8.85 and can be paired with their 170g Sage and Onion Stuffing Mix for just 45p. Yorkshire puddings (15 per pack) will be 46p and 300g of Gravy Granules (300g) will be just 99p. It is not clear when these prices will change. Richard Bourns, Lidl GB Chief Commercial Officer, sought to reassure customers that the reduction in prices are funded by the supermarket so farmers won't be paid less. Richard said: "With household budgets remaining under pressure we are on a mission to deliver unbeatable festive value to our shoppers this Christmas. "By pricing a complete Christmas dinner at less than £1.40 per head, we’re giving reassurance from the very start of the season that we won’t be beaten on price and we won’t compromise on quality. "We’ve already invested £400 million in lowering prices this year and we aren’t stopping there. "Between additional price cuts and a further £75 million in Lidl Plus savings in the run up to Christmas, we’re making sure British families get the value they really deserve. "No guesswork, no festive price shock - just unbeatable value that's locked in. "Crucially, that value never comes at the expense of producers and every penny of our seasonal promotions is funded directly by us. "That means we guarantee our farmers the same full, fair, contracted price they rely on throughout the season."

metadata.title: Rare Royal Mint 20p coin sells for more than 400 times face value on eBay
metadata.contentSnippet: A Royal Mint 2023 puffin 20p coin attracted 18 bids on eBay, before selling for more than 400 times its face value

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rare Royal Mint 20p coin sells for more than 400 times face value on eBay
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Royal Mint 20p piece desired by coin collectors has sold for more than 400 times its face value during The circulated Puffin 20p coin, which features King Charles III on the reverse side of the coin, sold for £82.08 on eBay, after sparking a mini bidding war with 18 bids. The Royal Mint records a circulation mintage of 525,000 for the 2023 puffin 20p. Its design features a puffin facing left, with a distinctive bill and detailed plumage, as part of a collection depicting British plants and animals. A 2008 20p piece is among the most sought after coins in the UK because of a minting error. It is known as a mule coin because an accidental mix-up at the Royal Mint left it with no date on either side. Featuring Queen Elizabeth II on the front, the coin shows part of the Royal Shield of Arms on the reverse. A production blunder occurred in November 2008 during a redesign of circulating British coinage, when an older heads die was paired with the new shield reverse. The Royal Mint confirmed that fewer than 250,000 coins out of 136 million 20p pieces struck in 2008 and 2009 were affected by the mistake. A spokesperson for the Mint previously said: "In November 2008 a number of 20p coins were incorrectly minted, resulting in the coins being undated. "This problem affected less than 250,000 coins of the 136 million 20p pieces minted in 2008-09." The 50 pence piece has become the most valued and collected coin in the UK, with many collectable designs appearing on its heptagonal canvas. Its 27.5mm diameter makes it the largest of any British coin, and allows space for decorative pictures. It has often been used to celebrate big events over the past 50 years of British history. The rarest coins tend to be of the greatest value, with the mintage (number of coins with each design made) being the fundamental attraction for collectors. Along with the design, other aspects of the coin which increase value are the condition of the coin and whether it has an error in its design. The way in which it is sold can also determine the coin’s value - while some coin collectors will bid vast amounts of money on eBay or at auction, others opt for more robust valuations by selling via a coin dealer. metadata.title: Wetherspoon rolls out change to policy in UK pubs after trial
metadata.contentSnippet: Wetherspoon has introduced a change across its pubs after a trial at 88 venues. Here is what the change means.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Wetherspoon rolls out change to policy in UK pubs after trial
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Wetherspoon is introducing a change across its UK pubs after a successful trial at 88 venues. The pub chain is changing how it maintains urinals, using a biological treatment called URIZAP, which is designed to tackle the build-up that can cause blockages and smells in men's toilets. The change covers its pubs in the UK and Ireland, and the company told the Mirror that the rollout was completed around July. It is a change to washroom maintenance rather than a new rule that customers must follow. The treatment comes from Thrive, a Lancashire-based company which began in a Lancaster University laboratory in 2019, according to Wetherspoon's magazine. Its scientists developed the product as an alternative to chemical cleaners used to deal with uric scale and blockages in urinals. The formulation works by digesting uric acid build-up and can be used in all types of urinals. Thrive says the treatment clears urinals and pipes at source instead of simply masking odours. Wetherspoon says the product is suited to busy washrooms and reduces the need for strong-smelling chemical cleaners traditionally used in such venues. In its winter and spring 2026/27 magazine, the chain said pubs using the treatment had reported a marked reduction in plumbing maintenance visits. The Mirror reported that staff at the 88 trial pubs noted improved odours, fewer maintenance issues and the removal of scale build-up from urinal pipework. Wetherspoon says the aim is to deal with problems before they arise, rather than waiting until a blockage needs attention. That matters during busy periods, when a urinal problem can pull employees away from serving customers or other work, according to the company. The chain says the treatment's continuous action can free staff to concentrate on other tasks and help avoid urinals being shut off at busy times. Wetherspoon also links the change to its sustainability ambitions, saying reduced reliance on chemical-based cleaners means fewer single-use plastic containers and lower volumes of chemicals entering wastewater. The company says the treatment allows it to make use of low-flush systems already installed in its washrooms to reduce water consumption. It has not given figures in the magazine for the amount of water, plastic or chemicals saved by the switch. Wetherspoon said: "Urinal issues generally demand attention at the worst-possible moments, pulling staff away from serving customers or other duties to deal with issues. URIZAP's continuous action frees staff to focus on other tasks." Vince Graham, chief executive of Thrive, said: "Wetherspoon leads the way on washroom standards. We're proud that one of Britain's best-known hospitality businesses has chosen URIZAP to take that standard even further, improving facilities for customers and staff." For customers, the intended result is fewer odours and fewer occasions when urinals need to be taken out of use for maintenance.

metadata.title: Center Parcs introduces new £5 rule for all guests at UK holiday parks
metadata.contentSnippet: Center Parcs has introduced a new £5 rule at all of its UK holiday parks, which came into effect across all its resorts on November 16.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Center Parcs introduces new £5 rule for all guests at UK holiday parks
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Center Parcs has introduced a new rule at all of its UK holiday parks. Guests will now have to pay a deposit to reserve tables at resort restaurants. A new policy, which came into effect across all its resorts on November 16, requires guests to pay a £5 deposit per person when booking a restaurant. The change is designed to reduce no-shows and ensure that tables are kept full. A statement on the Center Parcs website read: "To help us provide the best possible experience for our guests and make sure our restaurants are available for as many guests as possible, all restaurant bookings now require a deposit at the time of booking. "This will come into effect for all breaks starting from 16th November 2026 onwards. "If your plans change, you can cancel more than 48 hours before your reservation, and we’ll refund your deposit in full. "If you cancel within 48 hours of your reservation, the deposit is non-refundable. "Please note that restaurant bookings have their own cancellation terms, which are different from those for activity bookings." Affected venues include Huck’s American Bar & Grill (all sites), Rajinda Pradesh (all sites), The Pancake House (all sites) and Foresters’ Inn at Longleat and Elveden. The deposit is fully refundable if the booking is cancelled more than 48 hours in advance. Guests are still welcome to walk in without a reservation, but availability cannot be guaranteed. It is not the only change at Center Parcs sites in the UK in 2026, with its crèche services axed earlier this year. The price was around £30 a session and was for kids between three months and three years, for up to three hours. However, the service is no longer offered at any of its five UK resorts. A spokesperson for Center Parcs said at the time: "We’re always looking to review and evolve the guest experience. We have made the decision to remove the crèche activity from our breaks, to reflect guest feedback and limited demand for this particular activity. "Crèche sessions are one of more than 20 activities available within our Activity Den and our other activities will continue to run as normal." There are five Center Parcs holiday villages in the UK. The company's first village opened near to Sherwood Forest, Nottinghamshire, in 1987. Each site offers woodland lodges, a Subtropical Swimming Paradise, an Aqua Sana Forest Spa, and car-free forest paths Have you visited Center Parcs before? Let us know in the comments.
